text: A group G (in HoTT) is defined as an h-set with group operations. Why the h-set requirement?
choices: Without h-set, the group axioms are not unique (multiple proofs of commutativity)
explanation: If G were not a set, the carrier would have higher homotopy, and there could be multiple inequivalent proofs of the group axioms. The h-set condition ensures a 'discrete' algebraic structure.
